title: Anthropic activates ASL-3 protections
summary: Anthropic introduced stronger safeguards for Claude Opus 4 because it could not confidently rule out relevant biological risk. A precautionary decision does not establish a demonstrated weapon.

title: Researchers argue models increase biological risk
summary: Roger Brent and T. Greg McKelvey Jr examine model guidance and argue that it can increase biological risk. This research preprint presents model dialogues, not a demonstrated attack.

title: CSIS considers stronger biosecurity safeguards
summary: A policy analysis considers how falling informational barriers could change biological risk and calls for stronger safeguards.

title: Dario Amodei sets out risks from powerful AI
summary: The Anthropic CEO's essay considers risks including biological misuse. It presents forecasts and arguments about future capabilities.

title: Nature examines the biological AI access debate
summary: A science news feature considers AI, biological design, and the debate over access. The linked article may require a subscription.

title: AI leaders join a call for biological safeguards
summary: WIRED reports on a letter urging stronger safeguards against AI-assisted biological weapons, signed by AI leaders and scientists.

title: Examining the evidence behind executive warnings
summary: The Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists critically examines warnings about AI-assisted bioterrorism and their likelihood.
source: Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists · Analysis

title: RAND proposes a layered biosecurity strategy
summary: A policy report describes nine mutually reinforcing mitigations for biosecurity in the AI era.

title: Anthropic publishes biological case studies
summary: The company reports five biological case studies and explicitly does not assert that the researchers intended harm. These are company findings, not independently proved terrorist plots.

title: Could AI build a bioweapon?
summary: A GZERO World interview examines AI and biological risk. Watch the 26-minute programme at PBS and hear the discussion in its original context.
